summary: Canonical, teaching-grade SOX agent in Python — the executable answer to 'how do I write a SOX agent?'. Runs both as a standalone script and as a Claude Code agent. Heavily annotated (≥1 comment line per 3 code lines). Owns three primitive coverage slots in the four-demo split: namespace (bootstrap connects to a named namespace), reply_to threading (thread_handling step demonstrates clarification_request → reply pattern), and channels_ack (ack_nack step demonstrates the tool-not-message ACK lifecycle). Heartbeat is emitted but the visual roster lives in chat-tui-demo; replay is used for recovery here, but the user-visible scrubber lives in chat-webapp.

lifecycle.annotation: PRIMITIVE COVERAGE: namespace. Connect to a named namespace passed via --namespace (default 'reference'); call list_channels first to verify _sox_protocol version compatibility (fail-fast on mismatch); subscribe to ticket:*, dm/<self>~*, sox/presence; emit first heartbeat to register as online. Drain any pre-existing messages from prior sessions before entering main loop.

Pull-based drain with cadence; track last seen seq PER CHANNEL in a dict for replay-on-recovery; flip presence to busy while processing a message; on each drained message issue channels_ack(received) immediately, then channels_ack(processing) on entering work.

PRIMITIVE COVERAGE: reply_to threading. Demonstrates the clarification_request → clarification_reply pattern. Use thread_depth=-1 on recv to pull full ancestor chain inline; reply via send with reply_to set to the parent message_id and channel preserved (replies stay on the same channel, not a sub-channel). Showcases the speculative-execute discipline: continue under best-guess assumption, integrate the late-arriving reply non-destructively.

PRIMITIVE COVERAGE: channels_ack. Demonstrates ALL four status transitions of the forward-only state machine. CRITICAL: ACK is a TOOL CALL — no body.type=sox-ack message is ever sent to a channel. After ACKing done, a subsequent recv MUST NOT return the ACK as a channel message. NACK path includes a reason string and is exercised by a deliberately rejected message in the integration test.

Background asyncio task fires channels_heartbeat every 10 seconds (the spec-recommended interval). Status reflects current activity: online when idle, busy when mid-task. Subscription to sox/presence is established in bootstrap; received presence events are logged but rendering is the TUI's job.

Refuse to stop while any pending message has only channels_ack(received) or channels_ack(processing) — must reach done or nack first. On clean stop: emit channels_heartbeat(offline), then unsubscribe, then exit. SIGTERM handler triggers the same path.

On agent restart (or after a context reset that loses in-process queue state): for every previously-subscribed channel, call replay(since=last_seq_persisted_to_disk) until has_more=false; then resume the main loop. State file at $XDG_STATE_HOME/sox-reference-agent/seq.json holds {channel: last_seq}. This is the canonical recovery recipe.

files.purpose: fully-annotated reference implementation; one section per lifecycle step, comment density ≥1:3
public_api: async def run()  # composes bootstrap → recover → main_loop with heartbeat task

files.purpose: argparse entry point: --namespace, --agent-id, --base-url, --credential-file, --state-dir, --once (run a single drain and exit, used by run_standalone.sh)
persist/load {channel: last_seq} JSON file for the recovery step; atomic rename on write

prose teaching walkthrough mirroring lifecycle[]; one H2 per step; explains WHY each call is made, not just WHAT; cross-links to spec/primitives/*.md; final section: 'Anti-patterns we deliberately avoided' (e.g. ACK as channel message)
quick-start: starts an in-memory backing-store SOX server in the background, launches reference-agent in --once mode against it, sends a self-message, asserts it round-trips, exits 0 within 30s
Claude Code agent definition: name, system prompt, tool list (the 8 SOX MCP tools + Read/Write), profile, lifecycle hints
isolated example package; depends on sox-protocol (workspace path); pinned for reproducibility
list_channels handshake, subscribe patterns, version-mismatch fail-fast, namespace propagation
drain → process → ack(received) → ack(processing) → ack(done); verifies seq state advances
reply with reply_to=parent.message_id; thread_depth=-1 returns full ancestor chain; replies stay on same channel
all four status transitions; ACK never appears in subsequent recv (asserts no body.type=sox-ack); forward-only state machine rejects backward transitions; NACK with reason
heartbeat fires on schedule; status flips online↔busy around handle_message; offline emitted on graceful_stop
kill agent mid-conversation, restart, assert replay(since=last_seq) backfills missed messages and no duplicates leak through
spin up reference-agent + a partner agent; run a scripted clarification_request/reply exchange end-to-end via SOX; assert outcomes

primitive_coverage: channels (bootstrap subscribe/recv/send), sequence-numbers (last_seq persistence + replay cursor in recovery), threads (thread_handling step, reply_to + thread_depth=-1), dms (subscribed in bootstrap as dm/<self>~*; integration test exercises a DM exchange), groups (integration test creates a group and exchanges a message — covers group_create/invite/join/list_members), presence (presence_heartbeat step), ack-nack (ack_nack step), namespace (bootstrap step, --namespace flag), pending-state (implicit via ack lifecycle), trace-ids (correlation_id passed through on all requests)
annotation_density: 1 comment line per 3 code lines minimum (excluding tests); enforced by a dedicated test in test_bootstrap.py that parses agent.py with `tokenize` and computes the ratio

risks.risk: ACK-as-message regression — new contributors might write body.type='sox-ack' out of habit
risks.mitigation: test_ack_nack asserts no message in any channel ever has body.type starting with 'sox-ack'; the README anti-pattern section calls this out explicitly
replay(since=last_seq) is exclusive (seq > since); state.py only persists seq AFTER successful processing; test_recovery asserts no duplicates

risks.risk: Heartbeat drift causing server-derived 'stale' state mid-task
risks.mitigation: heartbeat is in its own asyncio task with monotonic-clock interval, not gated on main loop liveness; status flips to 'busy' rather than skipping a beat

risks.risk: Standalone run >30s under cold Python startup on CI
risks.mitigation: run_standalone.sh uses in-memory backing store + --once mode; no network; single recv cycle; budgeted at 5s wall-clock

risks.risk: Annotation density ratio gamed by trivial comments
risks.mitigation: annotation test counts only comments ≥10 chars excluding shebang/encoding/copyright; reviewer-facing not just CI-facing

build_order: 10. tests in same order; coverage 100% on agent.py
exit_signals: annotation density test passes (≥1:3 comments to code)
Integration test green: agent + partner exchange a full thread
README walkthrough has one H2 per lifecycle[] step
Every spec/primitives/*.md file appears in primitive_coverage
